regime_context: The detector shows a broad, multi-theme rotation with no single dominant narrative. The momentum leader (Memory, HBM & Storage) is fading with low durability and negative short-term returns, while strong trend-health (high durability, broad participation) concentrates in Cybersecurity and Managed Care, both flagged as crowded. The absolute-trend gate, the only validated edge, favors risk-controlled exposure to durable uptrends—not momentum-chasing. Given a zero-earnings track record, any conviction must be low.
emerging_watch: Financials (Equal-Weight) — durability 0.83, hurst trend, breadth 0.895, not crowded. Watch for potential handoff if current tech/healthcare leadership erodes. Kill criterion: Financials' durability_bar drops below 0.6 or weekly XLF close below 20-week SMA.

theses.subject: Memory, HBM & Storage
theses.thesis: The momentum leader is fading: the detector flags it as 'fading' with a mixed hurst tag, durability barely at 0.5, zero breadth (0.0), and a negative 10-day return (r10: -0.1269). Under the discipline of the absolute-trend gate, this theme lacks the staying power needed to justify exposure—reduce until trend health improves, acknowledging that this is a momentum-fading judgment, not a fade call on crowding.
theses.dissent: Memory could be undergoing a healthy consolidation within a longer-term AI-driven capex cycle; underweighting at this moment might miss a rapid snap-back when HBM orders accelerate again, especially if the AI narrative re-intensifies.

falsifier.text: SMH ETF closes above its 50-day simple moving average AND the detector updates to show Memory, HBM & Storage durability_bar > 0.7 with breadth > 0.5 and hurst_tag reverting to 'trend'.
